description: Intent-anchored eval scenarios for the microsoft-todo connector arranged on the setup spectrum (arrange-act / discover-act / act-only) so a 3-arm run reveals native's capability profile; outcome assertions grade all arms, mechanism assertions our-arm-only. Run per the agentskills.io eval methodology.

evals.description: Guidance-derived: add a task without naming a list, then confirm it landed in the default list — probes the default-list shortcut without an extra list-lookup round trip.

steps.intent: Add a task to my to-do list: 'Buy milk {{run_id}}', with a note: 'Also get eggs.'

outcome: A task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' now exists with a note reading 'Also get eggs.' and its id is reported.
mechanism: Creates the task directly in the default list without first calling a separate list-lookup step to resolve a list id.

steps.intent: Confirm the 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' task is in my to-do list and not yet completed.

outcome: The task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' is found and its status is reported as not yet completed.

evals.description: Guidance-derived: create a task with an explicit due date/time, then read it back rather than assuming a naive round trip (documented due-date time-of-day quirk).

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Submit expense report {{run_id}}' due this Friday at 3:00 PM Pacific time.

outcome: A task titled 'Submit expense report {{run_id}}' now exists with a due date set and its id is reported.
mechanism: Sets both a date/time and an explicit time zone on the due date rather than a bare date string with no zone.

steps.intent: Read back the due date on the 'Submit expense report {{run_id}}' task and tell me exactly what's stored.

outcome: The reply reports the due date and time zone actually stored on the task, rather than just repeating the originally-requested value without checking.
mechanism: Re-fetches the task to read the stored due date rather than answering from memory of the create call.

evals.description: Create two tasks then list open (incomplete) items in the same list, confirming both appear.

steps.intent: Create two tasks in my to-do list: 'Draft agenda {{run_id}}' and 'Book room {{run_id}}'.

outcome: Both 'Draft agenda {{run_id}}' and 'Book room {{run_id}}' now exist as tasks and their ids are reported.

steps.intent: Show me my open, not-yet-completed to-do items.

outcome: Both 'Draft agenda {{run_id}}' and 'Book room {{run_id}}' appear in the reported list of open items.
mechanism: Excludes completed tasks from the listing rather than returning every task unfiltered.

evals.description: Find-then-act: create a task, find it by name, then raise its importance.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Renew passport {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Renew passport {{run_id}}' now exists and its id is reported.

steps.intent: Find the 'Renew passport {{run_id}}' task and mark it high importance.

outcome: The 'Renew passport {{run_id}}' task's importance is now high.
mechanism: Looks up the task by title before updating it rather than acting on a guessed or hard-coded id.

evals.description: Create a task then mark it done — the single most common task mutation.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: I finished the 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' task — mark it done.

outcome: The 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' task's status is now completed.
mechanism: Updates the existing task's status rather than deleting it or creating a duplicate.

evals.description: Guidance-derived: complete a task, then ask to undo that — there's no dedicated reopen tool, so the agent must recognize completion is reversed via the same update path.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Water plants {{run_id}}' and mark it done.

outcome: A task titled 'Water plants {{run_id}}' exists and its status is completed.

steps.intent: Actually, I marked 'Water plants {{run_id}}' done by mistake — undo that.

outcome: The 'Water plants {{run_id}}' task's status is back to not completed.
mechanism: Reopens the task by changing its status field rather than declining, deleting it, or creating a new task.

evals.description: Create a task then delete it.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Old reminder {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Old reminder {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: Delete the 'Old reminder {{run_id}}' task, I don't need it.

outcome: The 'Old reminder {{run_id}}' task no longer exists.
mechanism: Deletes only the task resolved in this session, not an unrelated task.

evals.description: Create a task then add several checklist items (steps) to it.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: Break 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' into these steps: book venue, send invites, order catering.

outcome: The 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' task now has three steps: book venue, send invites, and order catering.
mechanism: Adds each step as a separate checklist item on the task rather than putting them into the task's note text.

evals.description: Create a task with steps, check one off, then remove another — exercises both checklist-item mutations in one continuing flow.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' with steps: book venue, send invites, order catering.

outcome: The 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' task exists with three steps: book venue, send invites, and order catering.

steps.intent: I've booked the venue for 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' — check that step off.

outcome: The 'book venue' step on 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' is now checked off; the other two steps remain unchecked.
mechanism: Updates only the matching step's checked state rather than the whole task's status.

steps.intent: We're doing potluck instead — remove the 'order catering' step from 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}'.

outcome: 'Plan offsite {{run_id}}' now has only 'book venue' (checked) and 'send invites' (unchecked); 'order catering' is gone.
mechanism: Deletes only the matching step, leaving the task and its other steps intact.

evals.description: Create a new task list for a specific purpose.

steps.intent: Create a new to-do list called 'Groceries {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task list named 'Groceries {{run_id}}' now exists and its id is reported.

evals.description: Create a list then rename it — contrasts with the built-in-list refusal case below.

steps.intent: Create a to-do list called 'Groceries {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task list named 'Groceries {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: Rename 'Groceries {{run_id}}' to 'Shopping {{run_id}}'.

outcome: The list formerly named 'Groceries {{run_id}}' is now named 'Shopping {{run_id}}'.
mechanism: Renames the same list id resolved in this session rather than creating a new list.

evals.description: Create a distinctly-named list then confirm it shows up when asked to see all lists.

steps.intent: Create a to-do list called 'Side Projects {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task list named 'Side Projects {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: What to-do lists do I have?

outcome: The 'Side Projects {{run_id}}' list is included among the lists reported.

evals.description: Destructive, higher-scrutiny case: create a list with a task in it, delete the list, and confirm both the list and its task are gone.

steps.intent: Create a to-do list called 'Temp Project {{run_id}}' with one task in it: 'Kickoff notes {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A list named 'Temp Project {{run_id}}' exists containing a task titled 'Kickoff notes {{run_id}}'.

steps.intent: Delete the 'Temp Project {{run_id}}' list entirely.

outcome: The 'Temp Project {{run_id}}' list no longer exists, and its 'Kickoff notes {{run_id}}' task is also gone.
mechanism: Deletes the exact list resolved in this session rather than a different or built-in list.

evals.description: Guidance-derived, vendor constraint: asks to rename the built-in default list, which Microsoft To Do does not allow — the agent should surface the real failure rather than fabricate success.

steps.intent: Rename my default to-do list to 'Inbox {{run_id}}'.

outcome: The reply states the rename did not succeed and that the default/built-in list can't be renamed, rather than claiming it was renamed.
mechanism: Attempts the rename against the real default list and surfaces the resulting error rather than silently doing nothing or fabricating a success message.

evals.description: Graceful refusal: recurrence authoring isn't supported by the connector — the agent should decline clearly instead of fabricating a repeating task.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Water plants {{run_id}}' that repeats every Monday morning.

outcome: The reply states that recurring/repeating tasks aren't supported and does not claim a repeating task was created; if it creates a one-time task as a fallback, it says so explicitly rather than implying recurrence was set.
mechanism: Does not call a create or update tool with fabricated recurrence data to fake the behavior.

evals.description: Disambiguation: two tasks share the same title; asking to update 'the' task by that title should prompt the agent to disambiguate rather than silently pick one.

steps.intent: Create two separate tasks, both titled 'Follow up {{run_id}}'.

outcome: Two distinct tasks titled 'Follow up {{run_id}}' now exist, each with its own id.

steps.intent: Mark the 'Follow up {{run_id}}' task as high importance.

outcome: Given that two tasks share that exact title, the reply either asks which one is meant or clearly acts on both — it does not silently update only one without acknowledging that more than one match exists.
mechanism: Recognizes more than one task matches the given title before acting, rather than picking the first result with no acknowledgment.

evals.description: Search for a task that was never created; the agent should report it wasn't found rather than fabricate one.

steps.intent: Has the task 'Renew car registration {{run_id}}' been completed yet?

outcome: The reply states that no such task was found, and does not fabricate a status or details for a task that doesn't exist.

evals.description: Guidance-derived: moving a task to a different list has no single tool — the agent must recreate it in the target list and remove the original, and should not claim the original task id survived the move.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' in my default to-do list, and create a new list called 'Groceries {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' exists, and a list named 'Groceries {{run_id}}' exists.

steps.intent: Move the 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' task into the 'Groceries {{run_id}}' list.

outcome: A task titled 'Buy milk {{run_id}}' now exists in the 'Groceries {{run_id}}' list, and it is no longer present in the original list.
mechanism: Recreates the task under the new list and removes the original rather than claiming the same task id was relocated in place.

evals.description: Graceful refusal / roadmap gap: linked-resource details (e.g. an originating email) aren't exposed by any tool.

steps.intent: Create a task titled 'Follow up on vendor email {{run_id}}'.

outcome: A task titled 'Follow up on vendor email {{run_id}}' now exists.

steps.intent: Show me the original email that 'Follow up on vendor email {{run_id}}' links back to.

outcome: The reply states that this connector can't retrieve or show a task's linked source item, rather than fabricating an email reference.
